text:
maria.pm: Heads-up — we need to lock the long-term policy primitives that will guide multi-region + tenant isolation work. Target: H2 2026 launch criteria. Can we align on must-have milestones, customer-driven requirements, and a concrete definition of 'done'? @sophia.arch @dan.eng @ryan.sre

dan.eng: +1. My priorities: (1) a machine-readable policy contract (priority, affinity, fallback), (2) perf SLOs (95th/99th) for each policy mode, (3) cost guardrails. No last-minute scope creep.

sophia.arch: Draft proposal — reduce ambiguity by defining three primitives we can iterate on: Affinity, Eviction, Fallback. Each primitive exposes a small set of knobs: TTL, priority, weight, strictness. Example config (for discussion):
```yaml
policy: 
  name: tenant-affinity
  type: affinity
  ttl: 300s
  priority: high
  fallback: regional-fallback
  weight: 100
```
This keeps the model simple for both the control plane and runtime.

ryan.sre: Operational constraints: we need telemetry + a fast kill-switch per-tenant and per-route before any wide rollout. Canary criteria: 2 weeks without eviction incidents across canary tenants, synthetic traffic pass at 99th percentile, and runbook tested. Also need an automatic rollback path when region-level latency > X ms.

leah.sales: From customers: deterministic failover (not random routing), residency/geo hints for regulated customers, visibility into decision logs for audits, and guaranteed migration windows. Several larger customers will require migration support (data + cutover assistance).

maria.pm: Nice — can we convert that into acceptance criteria? My draft: 1) Policy contract proto + public examples, 2) Runtime implements affinity/eviction/fallback with opt-in toggle, 3) Telemetry: decision logs + latency/cost metrics per policy, 4) Canary plan + rollback playbook, 5) Customer onboarding doc + migration checklist, 6) SLA/rate of degraded requests tolerance defined. Thoughts? :spiral_calendar:

dan.eng: That looks fair. For scope control, propose an MVP that: a) supports per-tenant affinity + simple regional fallback, b) records decision logs to blob store (30d retention), c) exposes metrics for 95th/99th latency and token cost. Anything beyond (e.g., per-tenant bandwidth shaping) can be post-MVP.

sophia.arch: Agree on MVP. For later phases we can add weighted routing (traffic split), explicit priority classes for enterprise tiers, and eviction heuristics tied to capacity signals. Also recommend we build the policy DSL to be extensible (so we don't balloon variance later).

ryan.sre: Telemetry detail: decision logs must include policy_id, input hash, selected_backend, latency_ms, token_cost_estimate, and user-visible reason (e.g., "capacity-constrained"). Minimum retention 30d for initial launch, with tiered longer retention for enterprise. Also require an automated alert when fallback rate > 5% over 10m across production.

leah.sales: Important to call out migration SLAs in contract templates. Customers will want cutover windows and rollback guarantees. We'll draft a standard migration playbook with templates for SOWs.

maria.pm: Action items (owners & rough ETA):
- Sophia: finalize policy spec + DSL examples (ETA: 3w)
- Dan: perf targets + MVP implementation plan (ETA: 4w)
- Ryan: telemetry schema + runbook + canary checklist (ETA: 3w)
- Leah: customer migration template + ask catalogue (ETA: 2w)
I'll collate and propose a razor-thin scope for Q3 planning meeting.

dan.eng: Also call out a risk: model-specific kernel performance can change affinity SLOs. We should publish a compatibility matrix per model family.

sophia.arch: Noted. I'll add a "model-risk" section to the spec and propose a gating list (which models can be routed under which policy).

ryan.sre: Final note — we should schedule a dry-run cutover with staging tenants (simulate partial-region outage) before signing off. Suggest booking that after canary passes.

maria.pm: Excellent. I'll create a short RFC from this thread and schedule the sync with product/eng/ops for next Tue. If anyone has objections to owners/ETAs, call them out now. Otherwise I'll move forward. :+1:
